transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Evan Romero (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (HelixCare CTO), Ravi Menon (HelixCare Head of ML), Lena Park (HelixCare Security), Samir Gupta (HelixCare Platform)
Artifacts mentioned: Deck: drive.redwood/model-catalog-demo (link), Benchmark spreadsheet: drive.redwood/benchmarks/helix-sample (link), Security pack: redwood.com/security/pack (link)

Summary:
Quick demo of Redwood's model catalog in Console and API, highlighting how customers select open models, view benchmarks and the compatibility matrix for their on-prem / VPC constraints. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated, KMS integration, and next steps for a POC with HelixCare sample prompts.

Topics covered: model selection, quantization profiles, benchmark metrics (p99 latency, tokens/sec), compatibility by architecture & hw (A100 vs H100 vs M60-ish), Redwood Optimize suggestions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Sofia, AE for Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:08] Dana: Dana, CTO at HelixCare. We're evaluating inference platforms for clinical note summarization and triage routing, hoping to keep latency under 200ms in P95 for short prompts.
[00:18] Ravi: Ravi here, Head of ML, we'll be owning model selection and evals.
[00:22] Lena: Lena, Security. I'll be looking at SOC2, KMS, data residency questions.
[00:26] Sofia: Great. Marcus and Evan from SE will jump into the console demo.
[00:30] Marcus: Cool, I'll share my screen — let me know if the audio's echoing.
[00:34] [00:34] Marcus: Alright, so this is the Redwood Console, first tab is the model catalog. You can filter by license (open vs proprietary), architecture (decoder-only, encoder-decoder), and hardware compatibility.
[00:46] Samir: Can you show only open models? We want to avoid license constraints for now.
[00:51] Marcus: Yep, toggling Open Models — here you can see curated families: LlamaX, Mistral, Redstone (our internal naming for tuned variants), and community forks. Each model card has a benchmark snapshot — p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and a recommended quantization profile.
[01:08] Marcus: For example, LlamaX-13B-QLoRA shows 60ms p50 on H100 80GB with q4f16 and about 1.2k tokens/sec. Quick note: these numbers are representative and we always recommend running a customer-specific benchmark.
[01:22] Ravi: Are those benchmarks run with prefix caching? Our use case uses short prompts with conversation history; caching matters.
[01:29] Marcus: Good call. The benchmark tag indicates whether KV/prefix caching and packing were enabled. This particular card used prefix caching and a 32-token history. The bench sheet has raw runs. I'll share the sheet after the call.
[01:40] Dana: How do we know what will actually run in our VPC? We have strict network rules and plan to deploy private nodes.
[01:47] Evan: The compatibility matrix is the second view — it maps model architecture and operator support to binary/runtime profiles on different hardware and docker images. For private deployments we produce a validated matrix that shows which quantized kernels are supported on your chosen hardware; if there's a mismatch we offer a fallback variant or a compilation path.
[02:05] Lena: Regression: we need to ensure no secret keys are leaked in logs and KMS integration for envelope encryption. Does the catalog expose any keys?
[02:13] Marcus: No keys are exposed in the console. KMS integration is supported — we can route model keys to your KMS (wrap/unwrap) and logs only contain token counts by default. We have an enterprise security pack with audit log configuration and HSM options; I'll send that.
[02:29] [02:29] Dana: Can you walk us through selecting a model for our triage workflow? Latency is priority but we also need medical-grade output quality.
[02:36] Marcus: Sure. Step one is to filter by open models that have good ROUGE/BLEU/eval snapshots for clinical summarization if you have evals. In the console we can attach your eval suite — you upload prompts and reference outputs and we'll score models across BLEU / Rouge / factuality heuristics. If you don't have an eval set, we recommend a small prompt sampling to start.
[02:55] Ravi: Do you run hallucination metrics or factuality checks? Those are critical.
[02:59] Evan: We have integrated eval metrics for factuality (entity overlap, entailment proxies) and a custom regression alert if a new model version drifts on those metrics. Redwood Optimize can recommend a model/quant profile that balances latency/cost with factuality.
[03:13] Dana: Show us the compatibility matrix again — specifically for on-prem A100 clusters.
[03:18] Marcus: Ok filtering by A100, shows models with tested kernels. LlamaX-7B runs with q4f16 and is validated; LlamaX-13B has a flagged path because some kernels need CUDA 12.2 bump. We annotate the matrix with action items: "needs lib update" or "requires kernel fallback".
[03:36] Ravi: If there is a kernel mismatch, what's the performance delta on fallback?
[03:40] Marcus: Usually fallback is 10-30% slower depending on op coverage. For 13B it was about 18% slower in our runs. That's why Optimize recommends either a smaller model or a different quant profile for strict latency SLOs.
[03:53] [03:53] Lena: On logging and compliance: can you outline retention controls and where logs live for Private?
[03:58] Marcus: For Private, logs can be routed to your ELK/Splunk via secure endpoints; retention is configurable at the tenant layer. Audit logs for key operations are kept separately and can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include the SOC2 checklist in the security pack.
[04:14] Samir: Back to the console — the model cards show a "Compatibility" tab with supported runtimes. Can we also get recommended hardware cost estimates?
[04:22] Evan: Yes, each model has an estimated cost-per-token bucket for hosted and for dedicated hardware (we estimate GPU-hours based on throughput and your expected QPS). Those are ballpark until we run a baseline on your exact workload.
[04:34] Dana: What's the process to lock down a model version? We need reproducibility for audits.
[04:39] Marcus: You can pin a model version and also pin a quantization profile. The Console stores the model checksum and docker image tag; when you rollout we capture the exact binary. There's an audit trail of deploys and canary results.
[04:51] Ravi: Can Optimize suggest a quantization profile automatically? For instance, if I want p95 < 200ms, can it pick model+quant+batching?
[04:59] Marcus: Exactly — Redwood Optimize ingests your workload signals (seq length distribution, expected QPS) and suggests a profile: model variant + quant type + batch/packing settings. It will also provide estimated cost and expected latencies based on prior runs. We can run a simulated batch with your sample if you want.
[05:15] Dana: That would be helpful. For HIPAA reasons, can we run that simulation in our VPC?
[05:20] Marcus: Yes, for Private deployment or Dedicated we can run the benchmark inside your VPC/cluster. For Hosted, we offer a contractual BAA and data controls, but many customers prefer Private for PHI.
[05:31] [05:31] Sofía: small interruption — (laugh) spelling my name — we will send a short checklist to determine hosted vs dedicated fit quickly.
[05:38] Dana: Perfect.
[05:40] Marcus: quick demo snippet — selecting the model, I'm clicking into the bench tab; here's a per-sequence length curve, and you can also toggle quantization comparison (q8_0, q4f16, int8). The chart updates with cost estimates and p95 latency.
[05:56] Ravi: How do you measure p95? Is it end-to-end including network?
[06:01] Evan: Benchmarks are measured within the runtime; for end-to-end we recommend you run a customer-specific test that includes network RTT and prefix-cache behavior. The bench artifact includes both isolated runtime numbers and an optional end-to-end measurement if the customer ran the script.
[06:16] Lena: A couple security specifics: SSO/SAML supported? RBAC for model access?
[06:20] Marcus: Yes SSO with SAML and SCIM, RBAC is supported per route and per model. You can restrict who can deploy or who can view bench data. We also support tenant-scoped encryption keys and optional HSM integration.
[06:33] Dana: For the POC, we want to test two models: a tuned LlamaX-7B and LlamaX-13B with q4f16. Can we compare in the Console?
[06:41] Marcus: I'll set up a side-by-side comparison — the Console allows paired evaluation. We'll run both under your seq distribution and record p95 and Rouge/factuality.
[06:50] [06:50] Samir: Any mention of fallback to smaller models under load? We want graceful degradation.
[06:54] Evan: Smart routing policies can do that — route by route you can set a fallback chain (13B -> 7B -> 3B) and set thresholds for latency or error-rate before falling back. This is in the runtime and the console shows route-level SLOs and fallback behavior.
[07:08] Dana: Great. About costs: can you provide a deterministic cost estimate for 100 qps with avg 40 tokens per request?
[07:15] Marcus: I'll record that as a follow-up but the bench sheet has cost-per-token numbers; with our ballpark numbers, 13B q4f16 on H100 would be ~ $0.0018 per token (hosted estimate) — rough. We'll give you a tailored estimate after we run your workload sample.
[07:31] Ravi: Do you support model customization or fine-tuning on Dedicated? We might prefer local tuning for privacy.
[07:36] Marcus: We support fine-tuning workflows; for Private deployments you can run fine-tuning pipelines on your infra. For hosted, we have managed fine-tuning options with controls. For many customers we recommend LoRA-style adapters or QLoRA for efficiency.
[07:48] [07:48] Lena: One more compliance question — where are embeddings stored if we use the embeddings API?
[07:53] Evan: Embeddings storage is configurable; by default in Hosted we store metadata only and hashed embeddings, but you can opt to persist them to your VPC or dedicated storage solution. We'll include this in the security docs.
[08:05] Dana: Okay, let's talk timeline and POC scope. We want a 4-week POC: week 1 onboarding and sample runs, week 2 benchmarks & tuning, week 3 integration, week 4 wrap + exec review. Is that feasible?
[08:18] Sofia: Absolutely feasible. For that we'll need your sample prompts and a small dataset plus access window for an on-prem benchmark if you're doing Private.
[08:26] Dana: I'll coordinate that — Ravi and Samir will handle dataset prep.
[08:30] Marcus: I'll put together a benchmark runbook and the spreadsheet we discussed.
[08:35] [08:35] Quick screenshare glitch, apologies — switching windows.
[08:40] Marcus: Back — here's the API quickstart: a simple POST to /v1/generate with model name, inputs, and route id. We have SDKs too. Demo: curl example, and a streaming websocket example for low-latency UI.
[08:55] Ravi: Is streaming over TLS only? We need to ensure persistent connections can be proxied through our LB.
[09:00] Evan: Streaming uses wss over TLS; we support common proxy setups and have documentation for timeouts and connection pooling.
[09:08] Lena: For private deployments, the console is either self-hosted or a thin control plane? How does control plane access work?
[09:14] Marcus: For Private we provide a control plane that can be run in your network; there's also a hosted control plane option with private connectivity. You can restrict telemetry and opt out of sending metrics.
[09:25] Dana: Could you illustrate the compatibility matrix export? We need the matrix for our procurement team.
[09:31] Marcus: Sure — export is CSV/Excel, includes tested CUDA/driver versions, op coverage notes, and recommended kernel versions. I'll attach that export.
[09:40] [09:40] Samir: Are there any known gotchas for NVIDIA driver versions? We run mixed A100 and older V100 in dev.
[09:45] Marcus: V100 lacks some fused kernels; we flag that in the matrix. For production we recommend at least A100 or H100 depending on throughput. If you have mixed infra, we can present a cross-compatibility plan.
[09:58] Ravi: For inference correctness, how do we guard against tokenization differences between model variants?
[10:03] Evan: The console normalizes tokenization metadata; we store tokenizer versions and checksum per model. When you run evals we compute metrics using the model's tokenizer to avoid mismatch.
[10:13] Dana: This is great. Any immediate blockers you see for HelixCare?
[10:17] Marcus: Only the compliance answers and your sample prompt set. Technical-wise, we've validated the kernels for the models you've expressed interest in except the 13B CUDA version issue I mentioned — that's a quick driver bump or we can run a fallback.
[10:31] Lena: I'll send the SOC2 scope and a list of questions by Monday.
[10:36] Sofia: Noted. Marcus — can you capture the tech follow-ups?
[10:40] Marcus: Yep — I'll add those items to the sheet.
[10:44] [10:44] Closing: Sofia: Recap quick: we'll send pricing/pilot agreement, security pack, bench spreadsheet, compatibility CSV; HelixCare to provide sample prompts and dataset; SEs to run benchmark in your target environment. Any other items?
[10:59] Dana: No, that's it — thanks.
[11:02] Ravi: Thanks, everyone.
[11:05] Lena: Thanks.

End of recording.
